# table-pipe-style

- ID: `MD055`
- Category: Tables
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: no
- Tags: `table`

Table rows use leading and trailing pipes the same way throughout.

## Why

Consistent pipes make tables easier to read in the source. Some parsers also
have trouble with tables that leave out the outer pipes.

## Options

Set them under `rules.table-pipe-style.options`.

- `style` (`string`, default `consistent`): Pipes to require at the start and
  end of table rows. consistent takes those of the first row. Values:
  `consistent`, `leading_only`, `trailing_only`, `leading_and_trailing`,
  `no_leading_or_trailing`.

## Fix

There is no automatic fix.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Rules

| Name | Fixable |
| --- | --- |
| line-length | no |
| no-hard-tabs | yes
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
6:20 Missing trailing pipe: expected leading_and_trailing, found leading_only
```

This document follows the rule:

```markdown
# Rules

| Name | Fixable |
| --- | --- |
| line-length | no |
| no-hard-tabs | yes |
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  table-pipe-style:
    options:
      style: consistent
```

Under `rules`, `table-pipe-style: false` turns the rule off and
`table-pipe-style: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable table-pipe-style` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line table-pipe-style -->
```
